commits.message:
Delete the watcher's unused replay generation

The watcher decides faults from the fault-proofs replayed ledger and
classifyHeader. Its own block replay, Phase A verifier, header-root
reconstruction and authenticated replay transcript in src/verification,
and the replay-transcript store in src/storage, were reached only through
the package index and their own tests. Nothing wrote a transcript: the
decision driver only retired, reset and completed operations against an
empty store.

Removed with them:
- the decision driver's retirement stage and the readiness reasons
  watcher_retirement_reset_failed and watcher_retirement_reset_pending;
  the handled-generation marker now moves as soon as a pass has pulled
  the generation;
- the replayTranscriptStore dependency of the fault-proof application,
  which now completes a workflow with verifyCompletedFraudProofWorkflow
  alone;
- the forced operator verdict spelling in user-event.ts, which only the
  replay records used;
- the tests and fixtures of the above, and their entries in the duration,
  module-size and lint baseline lists.

Kept: the rule bundle, user events, and openWatcherSqliteDurableBackend,
which still refuses a non-durable or symlinked store path at startup and
sets the journal mode. Existing databases keep their now unread
watcher_replay_transcript tables.

midgard-node-tools' public DA test built its empty block from a deleted
watcher fixture; it now builds the payload itself.

Restore a reservation's collateral before an action when what remains is short

A confirmation releases only the collateral coins its transaction named. A
reservation whose collateral took two coins (a removal's collateral is the
slashing penalty's percentage) kept the other coin, and the next action began
without refreshing because some collateral remained. A removal then needed
more collateral than the restricted wallet offered, Lucid took a reserved
funding coin as collateral, and preparation refused the transaction.

The next action now refreshes the idle reservation whenever its collateral is
short of what the planner reserves: the largest of the release floor, an
ordinary action's collateral and a removal's. A refusal of the separation now
names each out-ref that broke it and on which side.

Prove a same-block withdrawal rather than the input's ledger absence

A spend or reference of an output a valid withdrawal of the same block
removed is also absent from the event's pre-state ledger, so both families
find it at the same event. Rank withdrawnInput ahead of nonExistentInput and
withdrawnReferenceInput ahead of noReferenceInput, as the existing doubleWithdraw
and NoIdx promotions do. An input absent for any other reason stays with the
ledger-absence family.

Leave an included correction alone until its block leaves the chain or settles

An objective whose last outcome is an included but not yet final
correction was queued again on every follower change until it was
recovery-deep, and each run captured and verified the same inclusion
again. Its outcome changes only when a rollback takes the inclusion block
off the chain, or when that block reaches completion depth. The progress
authority now reads the block's depth from the follower and queues such an
objective only then.

Keep a queued header's deadline on objectives no fault names

An objective with a signed attempt that no fault names in an observation
(after a restart, until the decision selects it again) was re-queued for
reconciliation with no deadline. Its maturity then dropped out of the
deadline health, the late-start readiness and the deadline alert, though
its header still bound it. While the header is queued, the re-queued job
now carries the deadline the header's queue node gives, the same one a
fault for it carries; a departed header still carries none.

Treat nothing as stable while the follower's chain is younger than the recovery depth

Signed-intent recovery read the release-final boundary with a lookup that
refused while the boundary lay below the follower's origin. Every passed
TTL or conflicting spend on a young chain then came back unavailable, the
workflow saw reconciliation as unknown, and the dead attempt was never
replaced. Below the origin no stored block is recovery-deep, so an expiry
is now expired_at_tip and a spend invalidated_at_tip, which supersede the
attempt at once; releaseFinalPoint stays the tip.

Check the confirmed_ledger root builders' heap in the default suite and move the at-size runs to the bench lane

The default suite now holds the two cheap bounds: the streaming trie
builder takes 1,000,000 leaves in path order in a heap that does not
grow with them, and the built root worker, driven through its message
protocol over 100,000 entries, keeps its heap after a full collection
within 4 MB from its first checkpoint to its last. Each fails against a
builder or worker that keeps the leaves or the entries.

The 1,000,000-entry worker run and the 300,000-entry paged verification
move to vitest.bench.config.ts (bench:confirmed-ledger:root and
bench:confirmed-ledger:verification), which CI does not run; the paged
test keeps its small cases. The CI file durations follow.

Let traced runs reach the mint-item honest-leaf refusals

The case table moves to a named constant so the traced-refusal planner finds the cases, and each leaf names the check that refuses it.

Verify confirmed_ledger in bounded memory and replay folds made during a run

The verification built its trie from the whole of confirmed_ledger held in
memory, so above a few hundred thousand entries every run failed inside
the worker's fixed heap and commits on landed tails waited for good. A run
now pages confirmed_ledger by outref inside its one repeatable-read
transaction: the worker hashes each page to leaves, which go to a temporary
table dropped on commit, and the leaves are read back in path order into a
streaming MPF builder that keeps one path of the trie. The tail root comes
from the same pass, merging each outref the landed deltas name into the
stream in path order. Neither thread holds the ledger, and the roots,
reasons, counters and outcomes are unchanged.

A fold that committed while a run was reading moved the frontier past the
generation the run recorded, and nothing applied it afterwards, so under
steady merging the record could stay behind the frontier. Every committed
fold now goes to a log of at most 256 folds. A pass is replayed over the
log before it is recorded, and the record after each fold, applying a fold
only when it read the candidate's generation, builds on its header, passed
the delta checks and carries the digest the pass checked. A pass whose
replay reaches the recorded generation replaces the record. A fold past
the cap drops the log and makes one full run due.

The runbook names the run, replay and overflow log lines.

Tests: the streaming builder gives the same root as the in-memory one for
random sets and for empty, single and long shared-prefix sets; the built
worker derives the roots of a million entries a page at a time, a size
the whole-ledger build could not reach; a run over several pages
finds a divergence on its last page; a fold made during a run is replayed
onto its pass, and a wrong digest, failed delta check or other parent
stops the replay; pushing past the cap leaves the record behind until the
due run, after which the commit builds.

Wait as pending for an unprocessed tail and judge payload faults before the parent ledger

A commit tail that landed-block processing has not reached yet reported
commit_base_ledger_unverified whenever the verified record lagged, though
what it waits for is processing. A header off the processed chain is now
off it whatever the verification, so the commit waits as
commit_base_pending.

Foreign replay checked the parent snapshot's root before the payload checks
that do not read the parent ledger (repeated keys, the DA commitment and
count). A block with such a payload fault on a diverged local ledger was
held as a local fault and retried instead of judged. The parent check now
runs just before the events replay, so those faults are invalid on any
parent ledger.

Tests: a header no processed row names resolves off the chain for a
missing, stale or other-generation verification; a payload with repeated
keys, or a DA count or commitment mismatch, replayed on a parent snapshot
that does not derive its root is invalid.
Refresh the min-ADA standalone transcript for the changed step scripts

Pin each absent-coordinate refusal to the check that refuses it

Traced runs now name the refusing expect for every new refusal, and the three harnesses that record publication fit skip that record under traced builds, as the other harnesses do.

Keep the absent-coordinate tests inside the lint and file-size limits

Sort two imports, move the in-layout field-length detection into the payload fixture, and split the forced-claim journey into its coordinate cases, its proof-material cases and a shared fixture module, wiring the new file into the Node CI journey list.

Hand the run head on with the record its watcher verified it by

A devnet family builds on the run's head: the healthy successor the previous family committed and its watcher verified. The watcher keeps verification records in memory only and never re-verifies a header an earlier process decided, so a family that opens a new session (a resumed or follow-up run) restarts the watcher and then waits for a verified record of its predecessor that never comes. The automatic decision stage timed out after 900 s even though the watcher had proved the fault and removed the header within a minute.

The head is now written with the successor's verified record, and each family's collector takes that record as it already takes an earlier attempt's retained ones. The record is still bound to the block's payload envelope.

Version confirmed_ledger by generation and advance its verification on a clean fold

A verification pass recorded only the frontier it read, so a ledger row
changed outside a fold, or a frontier unfolded and folded back to the same
header and root, still looked verified to the commit base. And every fold
moved the frontier past the recorded pass, so commits on landed tails
waited for the next full run after each one.

Migration 0038 adds a generation to the frontier, drawn from a sequence no
table owns, so it is never reset or drawn twice. Every frontier write draws
one, and a statement-level trigger draws one onto the frontier row for any
statement that writes confirmed_ledger, in the writing transaction. A
verification pass records the generation it read, and a commit builds from
it only while the frontier carries the same one.

Once landed-block processing commits a fold, the record advances to the
folded block, its root and the generation the fold left, when the fold read
the recorded generation under its frontier lock, the block's delta passes
the commit's apply checks, and the delta's digest is the one the last run
checked for that block. Otherwise the record is unchanged and commits wait
for the next full run. A pass from a run that read an older generation is
ignored; a divergence it finds is counted and logged, but raises nothing
and leaves the record.

Tests: the generation changes on each frontier write and each write to
confirmed_ledger, and survives a truncate with restart; a clean fold
advances the record and lets the next commit build without a full run; a
changed generation, a failed delta check or a different delta digest
leaves it; a lower-generation pass is ignored and a lower-generation
divergence is counted without touching readiness or the record.
